answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to post a stake that is slashed when fraud is proven, and by tying reputation to a graph of verified interactions. A new identity starts at the lowest vertex of trust and must climb a ridge of successful, attested work before it can trade at scale. Like a ferrous anchor, the stake makes mass-producing sock puppets expensive, because every fake identity must risk real collateral that is lost if peers detect duplicate or dishonest behavior.
